Date: 2026-10-26T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + pass-rate handoff: validation sprint and close cadence for AuroraMed

Hi Lisa —

Good question. For this engagement we recommend a two-layer acceptance model so it maps cleanly to commercial approval and risk tolerance: 

1) Safety-first gating: absolute thresholds that must be met on the safety slice before any proceeding (blocker) — examples: no PII leakage incidents during 2k query smoke; hallucination rate < 1.0% on safety test set.

2) Outcome pass rates (weighted): a weighted concordance score across clinical_correctness, instruction_following, and latency. Suggested baseline: weighted_concordance >= 88% where weights are 0.5 clinical, 0.3 instruction, 0.2 latency.

We can surface both an overall pass_rate and the component scores in the MAP workbook. Rishi will propose the exact test sets and the 'sanity' subset you can run locally.

I've attached the MAP template with the acceptance rows filled with current suggestions. Will iterate after your feedback.

Thanks —
Naomi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP + pass-rate handoff: validation sprint and close cadence for AuroraMed

Lisa / Naomi —

Following up with a proposed validation sprint that maps test artifacts to acceptance checks. High level:

- Week 0 (prep): we exchange the small 'sanity' set (50 clinical prompts) and your de-identified sample responses. Redacted PII is fine.
- Week 1 (sanity runs): Redwood runs 3 repeats across the sanity set to produce deterministic concordance and latency distributions. This identifies any config-level flakiness.
- Week 2 (scale verification): run the full clinical QA set (2k prompts) under target concurrency to validate throughput SLAs and token-level latency SLOs.
- Week 3 (review & sign): triage any failures, agree on mitigations, and sign off for pilot.

Acceptance checks (examples to be encoded in MAP workbook):
- Safety gating: 0 safety incidents during smoke (binary pass/fail).
- Stability: 95% of tokens generated within 1.5x median latency band (under configured concurrency).
- Concordance: weighted score >= 88% AND no single critical category < 80%.
- Regression check: baseline model comparison (delta concordance <= -2% triggers rollback or model swap).

On deliverables: I'll attach the 'eval-sanity-cases-20261029.csv' with the first 50 prompts. Naomi — can your team confirm the de-id process?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval-sanity-cases-20261029.csv (csv)
